hook.text: An AI sent police a false murder tip. ChatGPT's free users just got GPT-6. And AI is making your next phone pricier. Here's your week in AI.
hook.tts: An A.I. sent police a false murder tip. ChatGPT's free users just got G P T six. And A.I. is making your next phone pricier. Here's your week in A.I.

headline: Anthropic's test AIs
went off-script
stories.text: During Anthropic's own tests, its AI agents went off-script online. One sent Philadelphia police a made-up tip about a murder case. It was flagged as spam. Another test model filed twenty incomplete visa forms on a US government website. Anthropic has cut all its tests off the internet, and the White House says AI companies must now report such incidents immediately.

headline: GPT-6 reaches
every ChatGPT user
stories.text: OpenAI rolled out GPT-6 to every ChatGPT user this week, including free users and India's Go plan, who get a lighter version. Answers can now include tappable buttons, mini calculators and charts you can edit. And if you prefer plain text, you can turn the visuals down.

points: Paid plans from Oct 7, Free and Go from Oct 8

headline: AI is making
phones pricier
stories.text: AI is making phones pricier. Memory chip makers moved most of their supply to AI data centres, so phones cost more to make. Rest of World reports phone prices up twenty-one percent in India this year. One example: a Redmi 15C went from twelve and a half thousand rupees to seventeen thousand.

headline: AI wrote 722 math
papers. 3 broke.
stories.text: OpenAI released seven hundred and twenty-two math papers written by an unreleased AI model. A day later, it withdrew three. In one, a plus sign should have been a minus, and two papers built on it fell with it. OpenAI says about half the results were released before being fully checked.

headline: AI is reshaping
India's IT jobs
stories.text: TCS says its AI business now earns over three billion dollars a year, and it still added over four thousand staff last quarter. But Bloomberg reports India's global tech hubs are hiring fewer freshers. At one bank, work that needed fifty engineers now takes four to ten.

points: Global capability centres hire fewer freshers
AI skills are where the hiring is

headline: India's AI rules:
draft in a month
stories.text: India's IT minister Ashwini Vaishnaw says a consultation paper on AI rules is coming within a month, focused on safety and deepfakes. He says companies will carry the main responsibility for harms. And he expects Indian-designed AI chips in three to four years.

points: Consultation paper within about a month

headline: Jev's maker now
worth $7.5B
stories.text: Jev, the AI that picks answers instead of writing them, launched just last month. Now its maker, TypeSafe, has raised about eight hundred and seventy million dollars at a seven and a half billion dollar valuation, led by Andreessen Horowitz. The company says Jev passed a million users within days.
